input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The missing or invalid CA bundle path check in cert_verify emits warnings.warn instead of raising OSError, so the failure no longer stops the request.
- failure path: A user passes verify="/etc/ssl/missing.pem" (or certifi returns an empty path); only a warning is emitted and execution continues to configure the connection with a nonexistent bundle, producing a later, misleading SSL or TypeError at connect time instead of the clear OSError.

Reviewer finding
- description: When the CA bundle path is missing or does not exist, the code now emits a warning instead of raising OSError. Execution then continues with an invalid cert_loc.
- rationale: Trigger: verify=True and DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH is missing or invalid. Previously this raised OSError with a clear message. Now it only warns and continues, so the failure surfaces later as an obscure SSL error, or the bad path is used silently. The commit title only mentions removing an unused extraction call, so this is an unrelated behavior change.
critique: The finding identifies the same mechanism: the missing or invalid CA bundle path check now warns instead of raising OSError. Execution then continues with an invalid cert_loc and fails later with an obscure error. Its trigger (verify=True with an invalid default bundle) differs slightly from the label's example but covers the same code path, including the empty certifi path case.
